IR.rationale: A rising belly-to-policy spread together with a steepening curve marks a bear-steepening repricing of duration. Yield changes are autocorrelated and term premia adjust slowly, so this state carries information about subsequent bond returns.

B.rationale: Widening credit spreads alongside weak high-yield returns signal credit stress. Such stress triggers flight-to-quality demand for Treasuries and pushes down risk-free yields.

V.rationale: Elevated equity implied volatility indicates risk aversion and safe-haven demand. It is also associated with expectations of accommodative policy, both of which support Treasury prices.

AP.rationale: Weak domestic and emerging equities together define a global risk-off state. Stock-bond substitution in that state favours government bonds.

ST.rationale: Equity style factors have no clear mechanism linking them to Treasury and investment-grade bond returns.

FX.rationale: A weakening USD/JPY tracks falling US yields and yen safe-haven flows. It is therefore a market-based gauge of the risk-off and rates-rally state.

COM.rationale: Rising oil prices feed headline inflation expectations and inflation risk premia, which put upward pressure on nominal yields.

MC.rationale: Rising breakevens under loose financial conditions describe a reflation state. That state is associated with higher nominal yields and weaker bond returns.

ENDG.rationale: Bond markets display time-series momentum, so recent strong returns tend to persist over weekly to quarterly horizons.

IR.rationale: A rapid repricing of near-term policy expectations relative to the funds rate signals monetary-policy uncertainty. Such uncertainty propagates into rate volatility across maturities.

B.rationale: Widening Baa spreads mark rising credit risk. They raise the odds of large flight-to-quality swings in Treasury and IG yields.

V.rationale: High market volatility combined with high policy uncertainty indicates a broad uncertainty shock. Such shocks spill over into the volatility of rates markets.

AP.rationale: Equity sell-offs drive abrupt reallocations into bonds and raise bond return variance.

ST.rationale: Equity style factors carry no clear information about bond variance beyond what the other groups capture.

FX.rationale: Yen appreciation is a classic risk-off and carry-unwind signal. It coincides with turbulent repricing of US yields.

COM.rationale: Commodity slumps generate disinflation and growth scares. These cause sharp moves in breakevens and nominal yields.

MC.rationale: Elevated financial stress, built from spreads and volatilities, predicts turbulent conditions across fixed income.

ENDG.rationale: Variance is persistent but mean-reverting. A high recent variance relative to its history is informative about the next-period deviation from baseline.

IR.rationale: Bear steepening, in which intermediate and long yields jump relative to policy rates, is the typical state of a duration sell-off and term-premium repricing.

B.rationale: Strong high-yield returns with stable or narrowing spreads signal risk-on rotation away from safe assets. That rotation lifts Treasury yields.

V.rationale: Low risk aversion removes safe-haven support and accompanies compressed term premia. Compressed term premia are vulnerable to sharp reversals.

AP.rationale: Strong equity markets reflect growth optimism and outflows from bonds. Both raise the risk of large bond losses.

ST.rationale: Equity style factors have no clear mechanism linking them to bond tail losses.

FX.rationale: Rising USD/JPY accompanies rising US yields and widening rate differentials. It therefore reflects the yield-up state.

COM.rationale: Broad commodity rallies raise inflation expectations and inflation risk premia, which raises the chance of a sharp rise in yields.

MC.rationale: Rising breakevens signal inflation repricing, the main driver of large losses in nominal bonds.

ENDG.rationale: Negative bond momentum tends to persist, raising the likelihood of further tail losses.

IR.rationale: Falling belly spreads together with falling bill rates indicate the market is pricing monetary easing. Easing expectations support large bond rallies.

B.rationale: Credit stress drives flight-to-quality flows into Treasuries and is the typical setting for large rallies.

V.rationale: Spikes in equity volatility coincide with safe-haven buying and expectations of easier policy.

AP.rationale: A global equity sell-off is the classic state in which government bonds deliver large positive returns.

ST.rationale: Equity style factors have no clear mechanism linking them to bond tail gains.

FX.rationale: Yen strength signals risk-off flows and falling US yields.

COM.rationale: Oil declines lower inflation expectations and signal weaker growth. Both favour falling yields.

MC.rationale: Financial stress combined with deteriorating labour data signals a growth scare. Growth scares bring easing expectations and strong demand for duration.

ENDG.rationale: Positive time-series momentum in bonds raises the probability of continued strong returns.
